body:
Three texts are now on the table, and they converge more than they contest. All three treat the ambiguity diagnosis as plausible but unconfirmed. Both critics hold that the account's ordering did prescriptive work the stated evidence had not earned. And both press, in different vocabularies, a second axis toward the front: that the avoidance may concern the form and stakes of the conversations — ultimately what kind of household this is — rather than the vagueness of any words. Here is what I take, revise, and decline.

What the objection establishes. Two corrections stand. First, the account's test (specify two or three chores, watch recurrence) has less discriminating power than claimed, because reduced friction is compatible with resentment plus clearer paperwork; recurrence can migrate to fresh complaint items or return at the next schedule change. Second, the 'thin material' caution was licensed into an ordered plan the thinness did not support. I adopt both corrections. One part of the objection overreaches: its renegotiation reading — 'yes, and then my shift changed' — is not untouched by the account's remedy. The third column, what happens when someone cannot do it, is a renegotiation rule agreed before the fact, and it answers exactly that case. The objection retains full force only against the standing/legitimacy reading and the rival's deeper question. I decline the objection's proposed remedy, though not its diagnosis: promoting the conversational-form reading to first place ahead of any new evidence would repeat the unearned-priority move with a different hypothesis, and the objection's own self-caveat concedes ambiguity may be the plainest reading. What the diagnosis properly requires is a first move that gathers evidence rather than presupposing a frame.

What the rival adds. The unit-versus-privacy reading stays on the table as a standing competitor, not yet promoted. Two of the rival's instruments are immediately usable. Its discriminator — watch whether the withdrawing flatmate engages with a proposal's content or pulls back from the idea of any arrangement — costs nothing, because any proposal elicits a reaction, and it repairs the exact weakness the objection found in the recurrence test. The truce-shaped arrangements (owned zones, no in-the-moment negotiation) belong on the menu as a low-exposure option, with one amendment: un-audited zones fail publicly (bins pile up, pests arrive), so a truce needs a single unit-level element, a minimal hygiene floor fixed once, after which nobody negotiates anything in the moment. I decline the rival's proposed opener — asking flatmates cold what they take the flat to be. It is abstract, easily heard as an accusation, and spends goodwill that neither reading has yet earned; the rival itself concedes the material cannot confirm either one. The same information comes cheaper sideways. I keep the rival's own caution symmetric: truce shapes can shield a free-rider exactly as specification regimes can feel like audits, so load visibility has to be monitored under whichever arrangement results.

Revised sequence, with grounds. First move: one-to-one with the withdrawing flatmate, a small ask, and about the form of the conversations rather than any chore — what makes these talks something worth stepping away from, and what would make them tolerable. The same separately with the other flatmate, and no aggregation into a group decision afterward, since that would suppress exactly what needs hearing. Both critics converge that this is where the distinctive evidence sits; it is cheap and reversible; and it honors the objection's charge about ordering by earning order through data rather than by declaration. Second move: for two or three genuinely recurring chores, propose one small, explicitly revisable arrangement that includes the fallback column, presented as a truce offer with the owned-zones alternative on the table from the outset — so the proposal does not enact one side of the contested axis, which answers the rival's strongest point about specification not being neutral. Observe the response for content-engagement versus pullback-from-the-idea. Third, the monitoring protocol: recurrence on specified items; migration of complaint to fresh items; survival of the arrangement through the next schedule change; whether load redistribution is visible or merely hidden. Reading the results: content-engagement plus falling recurrence plus no migration supports the ambiguity reading for now. Pullback from the proposal itself promotes the household-meaning conversation to the front — on evidence, which is where the rival wanted it all along. Falling recurrence with complaint-migration points at load or resentment. Fourth, the threshold: if the withdrawing flatmate disengages from both the form-of-conversation check and a low-exposure proposal, name the living-arrangement question explicitly rather than iterating chore formats; the account's step five and the rival's r11 merge here.

What stays open. Whether past disputes were about meaning, bindingness after change, or standing to raise the issue is unsettled and my probe localizes future cases without settling the past. Whether the withdrawing flatmate will engage with anything at all is unknown; if not, no diagnostic works and the threshold governs. Duration and background grievances remain unreported, so everything above stays one careful iteration deep. Nothing here decides that the withdrawing friend is reasonable, or that ambiguity is the truth of the matter; the plan is built so that its first two moves are informative under every hypothesis currently on the table.
